t: Section 1009(c)(2) of the Legal Services Corporation Act (42 U.S.C. 2996h(c)(2)) is amended by striking out “The” and inserting in lieu thereof “Upon request, the”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment that makes an existing duty under the Legal Services Corporation Act apply only "upon request". The tempting reading is that "upon request" signals an outside party asking the government for something, but the text sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal parties, or right to sue. From background knowledge, the amended provision concerns submitting audit reports to the Comptroller General, which stays inside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “The” and inserting in lieu thereof “Upon request, the”.

opus.w: This technical amendment only adds the words "Upon request" to a provision of the Legal Services Corporation Act. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Reading "upon request" as participation fails because the text never says who makes the request, and the underlying provision seems to be about reports, which may go to Congress (inside the government), not about bringing outsiders into a federal decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking out “The” and inserting in lieu thereof “Upon request, the”
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading:** "Upon request" might look like an outside party can prompt the Corporation to act. That reading fails because the section names no requester and creates no consultation, hearing, comment period or advisory body. As best I recall, section 1009(c)(2) is about reporting to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The text shown doesn't confirm this, so my confidence is a little lower.
2. **The answer:** This is a one-word technical amendment, and it brings no one from outside the federal government into a federal decision.
